utterances.text: Yes. And I think I can probably do it in five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Bogdanovic, was your home very far from the school in Pilica, this Kula school?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: About how far was it?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: To my house? A kilometre and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what about Stevo Ostojic and Rajo Jurosevic? Did they live near to you?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: No. They are a bit further.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So that I understand the position, they came to your house and asked you to go to the Kula school; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because there were some people who had been brought there and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was that of some concern to the people who lived nearby to the school and in the area you lived in?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: But of course. Of course it was of concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And were you and Stevo Ostojic and Rajo Jurosevic worried about what might happen to people who lived nearby, including your own families?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Of course we were worried.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, do I take it that on that day, you were not required to go and report for duty at Branjevo Farm?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: We did and then Lakic told us to go to have a rest and then we all went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Did you regularly report for work at Branjevo Farm on a Sunday?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, regularly. But we didn't work on Sunday. We worked for as many days as the troops were on the line, and if they were on the lines for five days, we worked for five days. We worked in two shifts, 12 men in each shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So on occasion, it would be usual for you not to report for work on a Sunday and there would be nobody working at the farm; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you recall whether the day when you went to Kula school was a Sunday or not?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just one or two more questions, please, if I may. Did you only prepare food at the farm for the soldiers in your own battalion?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: The Pilica Battalion and the Lokanj Battalion. We dug potatoes, we drove those potatoes to the kitchen, we cooked them, and then we either used horses or tractors to distribute the potatoes and food from one trench to another. That's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you for that very full answer. And is it right that in July of 1995 you still regarded yourself as being part of the Pilica-Lokanj Battalion rather than any other?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Lastly this: Two questions. When you were in Pilica at the dom, it's right, isn't it, that the dead bodies represented a health hazard and a risk for the people who lived nearby there?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: But of course. And we did not have any protective means, no gloves. I came home covered in blood. I burnt my clothes. There was nothing else for me to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the people who lived nearby were very grateful that you were doing this and they gave you rakija to fortify you?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when you were there, I think you recognised some of the men in uniform as being the policemen who regularly came to get you if you didn't report for work, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them. I did not recognise any of our men. I don't know which brigade or battalion brought them over there. I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Bogdanovic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have a re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Bogdanovic, you told us about the nine bodies that you saw at the Kula school. Could you just tell us what kind of clothing those bodies had on? Was it military clothing or civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: JEVTO BOGDANOVIC
utterances.text: Civilian, civilian clothing. Boots. But they had lost them probably during the night when they were running and when they took these people away finally they had to drag the bodies away as well. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogdanovic. Thank you for coming to give evidence and on behalf of the Trial Chamber, I wish you a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to inform the Trial Chamber that the document that my colleague, Mr. Zivanovic presented, which is 1D112 [as interpreted], for which the Prosecutor asked for the source, this is in the Prosecutor's collection under the number DA176530. But I would like to raise the following issue. How come that this document has not been disclosed to us? Several people who resided in Srebrenica, and the Prosecutor says it is not important how many, it may not be important but we are talking about two facts on which decisions were made in the cases of Blagojevic and Krstic which were accepted as accepted facts in this case. Under 2, this document refers to the humanitarian aid and the humanitarian aid had to do with the counts in the indictment relative to my client. I know that the Prosecutor has a totally different concept with regard to Article 68, Rule 68, that is, and I know that some documents do not relate to that rule. However, irrespective of that, I believe that this document should have been disclosed to the Defence and now what I would like to ask the Trial Chamber to do is to order the Prosecutor to investigate how long they've had that document and also to disclose to us any other document relative to the number of people who resided in Srebrenica before its fall and all documents relative to the humanitarian aid. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau for that information and request. I think, Mr. McCloskey, we can adjourn today because our time is over, but we expect you to come back with your reaction to the issues raised by Madam Fauveau, and also, if possible, inform us whether you are aware of other documents, maybe in the same collection. Madam Fauveau, just to make sure, it is 1D312, isn't it, not 112?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, 1D312.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So we'll revisit this tomorrow morning. We are sitting in the morning tomorrow. You will all recall that. We'll have our next witness and then we can break for the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. We only have one witness left, as you may know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of May, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
